brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two full hex bases (0,0,0 and 1,0,0) side by side, end caps on the open faces, joints locked. It is a low two-cell unit with top surfaces, not a multi-tier bookcase. I didn't add books as props.

Two notch drawer frames: notch:0#0,1#notch1 and notch:0#1,-1#notch4. Each sits in the gap beside the two bases. The configurator offered no separate drawer sockets, so the drawers are the frames themselves.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It knows nothing about strength or load ratings, and the parts are 3D-printed plastic. I can't claim any rating, and nothing here is verified for 50 kg. Test it physically before loading it, or use a proper rated shelf.

finish.summary: I built a small two-cell hex unit with two notch drawers, end caps and locked joints. check_build reports no issues and the mesh check is clear. The build also raised a STABILITY_TIP warning when I added the first drawer, and I didn't act on it. The 50 kg load rating is unmet because the configurator can't verify it. The unit is also smaller than a typical bookshelf.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
